Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise breakdown of our current defaults for hosted API (we can change these for Dedicated/Private on contract):

1) Requests (raw prompts / user input)
- Default: retained for 90 days from ingestion for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Rationale: retains enough window to investigate incidents while limiting long-term exposure.

2) Final model outputs (finalized responses)
- Default: retained for 90 days.
- Note: final outputs are treated the same class as requests for default retention.

3) Streaming tokens / in-flight partial responses
- Default: ephemeral; kept in memory for the duration of the session and flushed on completion. Staging buffers persist for up to 15 minutes to recover interrupted streams, then are removed automatically.

4) KV cache & session state
- Default: KV cache is memory-resident and not persisted to long-term storage for standard hosted accounts. We snapshot session state only when you opt into session recovery (account setting). If you enable session persistence, snapshots are kept in your tenant storage and follow the tenant retention policy (default 90 days).

5) Embeddings
- Default: embeddings produced via the embeddings endpoint are NOT indexed or stored in a shared index by Redwood by default. We return the vector to the caller; persistent storage happens only if you call the optional "Indexing/Vector DB" feature or enable long-term embedding storage in account settings. If you choose to store embeddings with Redwood, retention is configurable (default 365 days for stored embedding indices unless overwritten).

Deletion / erasure evidence and workflow (hosted):
- Customer requests for account-level purges are handled by Support + Compliance. We run a coordinated purge job across services, generate a purge report (job id, affected object ids, timestamps, region), and provide a signed attestation PDF with the job id and a CSV of deleted record identifiers where feasible.
- SLA: typical turnaround is 48–72 hours for standard requests; expedited erasure can be requested under an expedited process in the contract.

EU residency specifics:
- If your tenant is provisioned in the EU region, all persisted artifacts (requests/outputs stored by default, indexed embeddings, snapshots) reside in EU-only storage. Deletion runs against the tenant-local storage and evidence indicates EU-region keys.

Examples (concrete scenarios):
- Example A (default hosted): a developer calls text-generation; prompt + final output exist in tenant logs for 90 days. Streaming buffer held 10 minutes then evicted.
- Example B (opt-in session persistence): session snapshots saved at 30-min intervals; snapshots kept per tenant retention (90 days default).
- Example C (embedding indexing opt-in): embeddings are stored in a tenant vector index kept 365 days by default; you can configure auto-purge to 30/60/90 days.

Audit artifacts we provide upon purge:
- Purge job id (e.g. purge-20261030-8317)
- Per-object deletion timestamps (CSV) or storage-level deletion markers
- Signed attestation PDF

I've attached our internal runbook that shows the purge steps and what evidence we capture. Happy to walk through it live.

Regards,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

- Can the EU tenant be configured with a 30-day auto-purge for requests/outputs by default? We need short-lived artifacts for the pilot.
- For evidence: is the purge job id something we can cross-reference via an API / audit log, or is it only in the attestation PDF?

Best,

Alice — short answers and next steps:

- 30-day EU auto-purge: yes, we can configure a tenant-level default of 30 days for requests and final outputs for the EU tenant as a pilot setting. Ben will confirm paperwork (we'll add this to the PSA/Order).
- Purge job visibility: we provide the purge job id in the attestation PDF and also emit a corresponding audit-log entry in your tenant audit stream. You can pull the entry via our Audit Logs API (we'll share the endpoint and example query).
- Customer-managed snapshot storage: yes — for Private and for Dedicated we offer a customer-managed storage option (S3/GCS) for session snapshots and indices. For hosted pilots we can enable an S3 export hook under an MSA addendum.

Next steps:
1) Ben will send an updated order addendum for the 30-day EU auto-purge and the S3 export hook option.
2) Kimberley and I can schedule a 30-minute walk-through of the deletion runbook and the audit-log examples (I attached a screenshot of the retention settings page showing the 30-day toggle).

Thanks — aiming to have configuration turned on by Nov 10 if the paperwork clears.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
